plan.contextChunk: This figure is a dimensioned elevation drawing of a natural draft cooling tower, rendered as a translucent orange solid of revolution. The silhouette is widest at ground level, sweeps inward to a narrow waist above the midpoint, then flares slightly outward again to a flat circular top. The left half of the shell carries many closely spaced vertical contour lines following the curvature, while the right half is left as a smooth tinted surface, and a row of small teal angled supports rings the open base. A vertical dashed line runs up the center as the axis, and a horizontal dashed line crosses it at the waist. Four measurements are marked with double-headed arrows: 72 m across the top rim, 60 m across the narrow waist, 79.6 m from the top down to the waist level, and 179.6 m for the full height from ground to top, drawn along a long dimension line at the far left. Placing both diameters and both heights against the same profile makes the whole shape recoverable from four numbers. The layout supplies the data for fitting a hyperbola, centered where the dashed lines intersect, to the curved sides of the tower.

elements: hyperboloid-of-revolution shell, translucent orange, waist at mid-height flaring to base and top
closely spaced vertical meridian contour lines hugging the left/front of the curved shell
central vertical dashed axis of revolution from base to top
horizontal dashed line crossing the axis at the waist (narrowest ring)
top rim circle (diameter 72 m)
waist circle (diameter 60 m)
base ring at ground level (widest, ~78 m)
row of small teal angled support struts ringing the open base
double-headed dimension arrow 72 m across the top rim
double-headed dimension arrow 60 m across the waist on the horizontal dashed line
double-headed dimension arrow 79.6 m from top rim down to waist level (right side)
long double-headed dimension arrow 179.6 m full height at far left
horizontal measurement line (slider-driven) sweeping the tower with a live diameter readout
2D side-profile hyperbola curve (right branch) shown in profile mode with the four dimension marks

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching from the translucent solid of revolution to the flat side curve reveals that the same four numbers (60 m waist, 72 m top, 79.6 m top-to-waist, 179.6 m height) fully determine the hyperbola that generates the whole tower

interactions.label: Height h (m)
interactions.teaches: Dragging the horizontal measurement line up the axis shows the diameter shrinking to 60 m at the waist (h=100) then growing to 72 m at the top, making the 1/Z-like hyperbolic radius change with vertical position concrete
Rotating the solid of revolution confirms the curved silhouette is identical from every azimuth — the tower is a surface of revolution of a single hyperbola branch

demo_steps.title: Waist (default)
demo_steps.narration: At h=100 m the measurement line sits exactly on the horizontal dashed axis-crossing; the readout shows the minimum diameter, 60 m.

demo_steps.title: Top rim
demo_steps.narration: Slide to h=179.6 m. The line reaches the top rim and the diameter reads 72 m, matching the top dimension arrow.

demo_steps.title: Base
demo_steps.narration: Slide to h=0 m. The diameter grows to about 78 m — the base is wider than the top, the hallmark hyperbolic flare.

demo_steps.title: Fitted hyperbola
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to 2D Profile. The shell collapses to one hyperbola branch with the 60 m, 72 m, 79.6 m and 179.6 m marks, showing the four data points that fix the model.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale 0.02 units per metre: tower height 179.6 m -> ~3.6 units tall (Y from 0 at ground to 3.592 at top). Hyperbola centred at the waist, which sits at h=100 m (since 179.6-79.6=100). With y measured from the waist, model x^2/30^2 - y^2/120^2 = 1 (a=30 m waist radius, b=120 m). Check: at y=+79.6 (top) x=30*sqrt(1+79.6^2/120^2)=36 m -> 72 m diameter; at y=-100 (ground) x=30*sqrt(1+100^2/120^2)=~39.05 m -> ~78.1 m base diameter. Radius at slider height h: r(h)=30*sqrt(1+((h-100)^2)/14400), diameter=2r. Radii in world units: waist 0.6, top 0.72, base ~0.78. Build the shell as a LatheGeometry revolving the right-branch profile (sampled h=0..179.6) about the Y axis. Colours: shell fill translucent orange #f3a878 opacity ~0.45, meridian contour lines #d97742, teal base struts #4db6ac, dimension arrows and text black #111, dashed axis/waist lines #444. In 2D Profile mode hide the lathe surface and struts, show the single right-branch curve plus the four double-headed dimension arrows exactly as in the source (72 m top, 60 m waist on horizontal dashed line, 79.6 m right side, 179.6 m far left).
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.LatheGeometry for the 3D shell so orbit reads as a true surface of revolution; keep meridian lines as a second wireframe-style lathe or as line segments at fixed azimuths on the front-left. The slider-driven measurement line is a horizontal ring/segment at height h with an HTML or sprite label showing the computed diameter to one decimal. For the 2D Profile toggle, set the camera to a front-on orthographic-like pose (or just hide depth) and swap geometry groups rather than rebuilding. Recompute the readout label reactively on every slider change using r(h)=30*sqrt(1+((h-100)^2)/14400).

authoredContext:
The design layout of a cooling tower is shown in the figure. The tower stands 179.6 meters tall. The diameter of the top is 72 meters. At their closest, the sides of the tower are 60 meters apart.

Project design for a natural draft cooling tower

A diagram illustrating the dimensions of a hyperbolic cooling tower, showing a total height of 179.6 m, an upper section height of 79.6 m, an upper diameter of 72 m, and a narrower waist diameter of 60 m.

Find the equation of the hyperbola that models the sides of the cooling tower. Assume that the center of the hyperbola—indicated by the intersection of dashed perpendicular lines in the figure—is the origin of the coordinate plane. Round final values to four decimal places.
